3:35.body: להברות means to give a mourner a light meal. Radak reports that the Sages read it as also written with כ, "to cut off": first the people wanted David dead, in the end they fed him. Radak says he never found that spelling in a careful copy.

sources.quote: כתיב להכרות בכ"ף וקרינן להברות בבי"ת בתחלה להכרותו ולבסוף להברותו
sources.says: Radak reports the Sages' reading: written with כ and read with ב, first to cut him off and in the end to feed him.

sources.quote: ואנחנו לא מצאנוהו בשום ספר מדוייק אשר ראינו
sources.says: Radak says he did not find it written that way in any careful book he saw.

sources.quote: להאכילו סעודה מועטת
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means to feed him a small meal.

4:1.headline: 'Saul's son' is not even named
4:1.body: The verse calls Ish-bosheth only בן שאול, 'Saul's son'. Metzudat David says that after Abner died, being Saul's son was the only strength he had left, so his own name is left out.

sources.quote: ועוד לא נשאר בו כח מלכות רק מצד היותו בן שאול המלך, לזה לא הזכירו בשמו
sources.says: Metzudat David says his only royal standing came from being Saul's son, so the verse does not use his name.

4:2.headline: They 'were' Saul's son's officers, or they killed a son of Saul
4:2.body: Rashi reads היו בן שאול as 'belonged to Saul's son', with 'to' left out. Radak brings Menachem, who read היו as 'broke': these two had once killed another son of Saul and fled for it.

sources.quote: הָיוּ לְבֶן שָׁאוּל
sources.says: Rashi says it means they belonged to Saul's son.

sources.quote: ומנחם פירשו היו כמו שברו וכן נהייתי ונחליתי ור"ל המיתו אותו
sources.says: Radak brings Menachem, who read היו as 'broke', meaning they killed him.

sources.quote: משרת עצמו ואחר עמו, כמו "ושני אנשים שרי גדודים הי' בן שאול"
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says a word in this verse serves both itself and the next word.

4:5.headline: The noon nap: the Targum calls it 'the sleep of kings'
4:5.body: Ish-bosheth was taking his midday rest when the killers came. The Targum calls it 'the sleep of kings', and Radak explains that kings used to sleep at noon.

sources.quote: וְהוּא שָׁכִיב יַת שִׁנַת מַלְכַיָא
sources.says: The Targum says he was lying in the sleep of kings.

sources.quote: ת"י שנת מלכיא כלומר כי מנהג המלכים לישן בצהרים
sources.says: Radak explains the Targum: kings had the custom of sleeping at noon.

4:6.headline: Not 'behold' but 'they': the killers came in
4:6.body: והנה usually means 'and behold'. Metzudat Zion and the Targum read it as 'and they', meaning the two killers.

sources.quote: והנה. כמו והמה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says והנה here means 'and they'.

sources.quote: וְאִינוּן אֲתוֹ עַד גוֹ בֵיתָא
sources.says: The Targum renders it 'and they came into the house'.

4:6.headline: Wheat buyers: a disguise, or an earlier murder?
4:6.body: Metzudat David says the killers got in by posing as men buying wheat, and Rashi says they came in with grain traders. Malbim reads the verse as an aside about an earlier killing in a wheat dealer's house, which is why they had fled.

sources.quote: שבאו תוך הבית ועשו עצמם כלוקחי חטים מאת איש בושת
sources.says: Metzudat David says they came in pretending to buy wheat from Ish-bosheth.

sources.quote: עִם תַּגָּרִים לוֹקְחֵי חִטִּים
sources.says: Rashi says they came in with merchants buying wheat.

sources.quote: כי עוד בהיותם שרי גדודים באו עד תוך הבית של לקחי חטים (בית המיוחד לסוחרי חטים) ויכוהו
sources.says: Malbim says this tells of an earlier killing they did in a wheat dealers' house.

4:6.headline: Struck 'in the fifth': a rib, or the side
4:6.body: החמש is a rare word for a spot on the body. Metzudat David says it is the fifth rib, by the liver and gall, and the Targum renders it 'the side of his loins'.

sources.quote: ואמר שהכוהו בדופן החמישית מול הכבד והמרה
sources.says: Metzudat David says they struck him at the fifth rib, opposite the liver and gall.

sources.quote: וּמְחוֹהִי בִּסְטַר יַרְכֵיהּ
sources.says: The Targum says they struck him at the side of his loins.

4:10.headline: Here בשורה means the reward for good news
4:10.body: The man who told David of Saul's death expected a reward. Rashi, Radak and the Targum read בשרה here as the gift paid to one who brings good news.

sources.quote: לְמַעַן תִּתִּי לוֹ שְׂכַר בְּשׂוֹרָתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says the man expected David to pay him for his news.

sources.quote: אשר חשב שאתן לו שכר בשורה
sources.says: Radak says he thought David would give him a reward for the news.

sources.quote: לְמִתַּן לֵיהּ מַתְּנַת בְּסוֹרָתֵיהּ
sources.says: The Targum says 'to give him a gift for his news'.

sources.quote: אבל בעיניו היה כמבשר לו בשורה טובה
sources.says: Malbim says that in the man's own eyes he was bringing David good news.

5:6.headline: Real blind and lame people, or statues that cannot see?
5:6.body: The Jebusites boast that even the blind and the lame could keep David out. A midrash reads them as statues of the city, which have eyes but do not see and legs but do not walk, carrying an old oath made with Abraham.

sources.quote: אמר בדרך הפלגה וגוזמא
sources.says: Metzudat David reads it as a boast: the place is so strong that even blind and lame men could stop David.

sources.quote: הֵם עֲבוֹדַת כּוֹכָבִים שֶׁלָּהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says the blind and the lame were the Jebusites' idols.

sources.quote: בעבור שבועת אברהם לאבימלך שהיתה כתובה בצלמים אשר שם שהם עורים ופסחים כי עינים להם ולא יראו
sources.says: Ralbag says they were statues with Abraham's oath to Avimelech written on them, called blind and lame because they have eyes that do not see.

5:9.headline: Why the place was called the Millo, 'the filling'
5:9.body: מלוא comes from the word for filling. Commentators disagree on what was filled: a ring of earth, a moat of water, or an open square that filled with people.

sources.quote: הֶקֵּף חוֹמָה נְמוּכָה, וּמְמַלְּאִין אוֹתָהּ עָפָר
sources.says: Rashi says it was a low ring wall filled in with earth into a mound.

sources.quote: ומלאו החפירה המים
sources.says: Ralbag thinks they dug a ditch around the fortress and filled it with water, which is why it was called Millo.

sources.quote: ואותו המקום היתה רחבה להאסף העם שם לפיכך נקרא מלוא
sources.says: Radak says it was an open square by the wall where the people gathered, named from the phrase 'call out fully' for assembling.

5:20.headline: Baal Perazim: the plain where God broke through like water
5:20.body: David names the place for how God burst through his enemies, like water bursting through a bank. Here בעל does not mean the idol Baal. The Targum reads it as a plain.

sources.quote: כְּמַיִם הַפּוֹרְצִים גְּדוּדֵי הַשָּׂפָה
sources.says: Rashi says the image is water bursting through the banks.

sources.quote: ת"י מישר פרצים וכן תרגם בעל גד מישר גד
sources.says: Radak notes the Targum renders בעל פרצים as 'the plain of Perazim', as it does with Baal Gad.

5:21.headline: Did David carry off the idols, or burn them?
5:21.body: וישאם can mean 'he carried them' or 'he set them on fire'. Chronicles says David burned the idols. The sages joined the two: they began burning them, and took the rest only after the idols were cancelled.

sources.quote: ושרפם, כמו (נחום א ה): ותשא הארץ מפניו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion reads it as 'and he burned them', like other verses where this root means fire.

sources.quote: ובדברי רז"ל וישאם לשון נטילה
sources.says: Radak says the sages read it as 'took', and explain that the idols could be taken once Ittai the Gittite, a Philistine, had cancelled them.

5:24.headline: Marching in the treetops: angels, or the wind?
5:24.body: David must wait for a sound of marching in the tops of the trees. Rashi says it is angels sent to help. Ralbag says it is wind moving the branches, so the Philistines would mistake David's steps for the trees.

sources.quote: הֵם מַלְאָכִים הַצּוֹעֲדִים בְּרָאשֵׁי הָאִילָנוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says the sound is angels marching in the treetops.

sources.quote: ימתין שיבא רוח יניע ראשי הבכאים בדרך שישמע בהם כמו קול צעדי המתנועעים
sources.says: Ralbag says David was to wait for a wind to shake the treetops so it sounded like marching feet.

5:24.headline: Read from the dog in Egypt that did not move its tongue
5:24.body: Commentators read תחרץ from 'not a dog shall move its tongue' in Exodus: move out, or raise a battle cry. A midrash reads it as 'decide'.

sources.quote: תנענע ממקומך להלחם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means move from your place to fight, as in the dog that did not move its tongue to bark.

sources.quote: תָּרִים קוֹל מִלְחָמָה וְאַבְחַת חֶרֶב
sources.says: Rashi says it means raise a war cry and flash the sword.

sources.quote: אז תחרץ דבר חרוץ הוא כמו אם חרוצים ימיו
sources.says: Radak brings a midrash that reads it as something decided, as in 'his days are determined'.

6:1.headline: One word, two roots: 'added again' or 'gathered again'
6:1.body: Radak says ויסף can come from אסף, 'gather', like ויאסוף. Or it can mean what it seems, 'he added', so David added to his gathering.

sources.quote: כמו ויאסוף שרשו אסף
sources.says: Radak says ויסף is like ויאסוף and comes from the root אסף.

sources.quote: כלומר הוסיף לקבץ עוד
sources.says: Radak says the plain reading is that David added to the gathering.

sources.quote: וַיֹּסֶף עוֹד דָּוִד. לֶאֱסֹף
sources.says: Rashi explains ויסף as 'to gather'.

6:2.headline: Baale-Yehuda is another name for Kiryat Yearim
6:2.body: Rashi, Radak and Metzudat Zion say this is Kiryat Yearim, which Joshua calls Baalah. Rashi adds that the word בעל here means level ground.

sources.quote: בעלה היא קרית יערים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is Kiryat Yearim, as Joshua writes.

sources.quote: וּ׳בַעַל׳ לְשׁוֹן ׳מִישׁוֹר׳
sources.says: Rashi says בעל here is a word for level ground.

sources.quote: ונקראת גם כן שם קרית יערים בעל
sources.says: Radak says Kiryat Yearim is also called Baal.

6:5.headline: Joy or play? The word for how they danced before the ark
6:5.body: Metzudat Zion says משחקים means they rejoiced. Malbim says it means they played in laughter, which was the fault, since they should have rejoiced with trembling.

sources.quote: משחקים. שמחים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion glosses משחקים as 'rejoicing'.

sources.quote: שהיו משחקים דרך שחוק לא כשמחים ברעדה
sources.says: Malbim says they played in a way of laughter, not as people who rejoice with trembling.

6:5.headline: An instrument whose name means 'shakers'
6:5.body: This word appears nowhere else in Tanach. Metzudat Zion says the instrument moves a person to shake his body and dance, and Radak gives two guesses at what it was.

sources.quote: יעורר האדם להניע גופו ולרקד
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it stirs a person to move his body and dance.

sources.quote: יניע אדם גופו בנגעו בו או הוא אשר בו יתדות ינועו בעת הנגון
sources.says: Radak says either it moves a person's body when he touches it, or it has pegs that shake while it plays.

6:6.headline: Nachon's threshing floor has a second name, Kidon
6:6.body: Chronicles calls the place Kidon. Radak says the sages held it was first Kidon, when Uzzah died, and later Nachon, because the Levites then carried the ark rightly.

sources.quote: והיא היא, ובשתי השמות נקראה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says Chronicles's Kidon is the same place, and it was called by both names.

sources.quote: אמרו בתחלה כידון ולבסוף נכון
sources.says: Radak says the sages taught it was first called Kidon and at the end Nachon.

sources.quote: לפי שעשו נכון שנשאוהו הלוים בכתפי
sources.says: Radak says it was called Nachon because they then did it right, with the Levites carrying the ark on their shoulders.

6:6.headline: Did the oxen slip, or did they shake the ark?
6:6.body: Radak first reads שמטו as something that happened to the oxen: their limbs gave way. Rashi, following the Targum, reads it as something the oxen did to the ark: they shook it.

sources.quote: כִּי שְׁמָטוּהוּ הַבָּקָר וְנִעְנְעוּהוּ
sources.says: Rashi says the oxen shook the ark.

sources.quote: שמטו פועל עומד כאילו נשמטו הבקר
sources.says: Radak says שמטו can be a verb with no object, as if the oxen themselves were loosened.

sources.quote: ולדעת יונתן שמטו פועל יוצא
sources.says: Radak says that in the Targum's view שמטו has an object: the oxen shook the ark.

6:8.headline: Angry at God, or angry at himself?
6:8.body: Metzudat David says David's anger turned on himself, like a man alarmed and shaken. Malbim says ויחר לו, unlike ויחר אף, turns the anger back on oneself.

sources.quote: על עצמו חרה
sources.says: Metzudat David says David was angry at himself.

sources.quote: כי זה ההבדל בין ויחר אף שיוצא לזולתו, ובין חרה לו ששב אל עצמו
sources.says: Malbim says ויחר אף goes out to someone else, while חרה לו turns back to the person himself.

6:10.headline: 'The Gittite' did not make Oved-Edom a Philistine
6:10.body: Gittite sounds like a man from Gath, the Philistine city. Rashi, Metzudat Zion and Radak say he was a Levite who lived in Gath.

sources.quote: עוֹבֵד אֱדוֹם. לֵוִי הָיָה
sources.says: Rashi says Oved-Edom was a Levite.

sources.quote: היה מתגורר בגת, אבל היה לוי ומן השוערים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says he lived in Gath, but was a Levite and one of the gatekeepers.

sources.quote: וקראו גתי לפי שהתגורר בגת
sources.says: Radak says he was called Gittite because he lived in Gath.

6:11.headline: 'All his house' read as his wife and eight daughters-in-law
6:11.body: The sages heard 'all his household' as a hint at one family miracle. His wife and eight daughters-in-law each bore six sons at once.

sources.quote: אִשְׁתּוֹ וּשְׁמוֹנֶה כַּלּוֹתֶיהָ יָלְדוּ שִׁשָּׁה בָּנִים בְּכֶרֶס אֶחָד
sources.says: Rashi says his wife and eight daughters-in-law bore six sons each in one birth.

sources.quote: דרשו ואת כל ביתו זה אשתו ושמנה
sources.says: Radak says the sages read 'and all his house' as his wife and eight daughters-in-law.

6:12.headline: Why 'for the sake of' the ark, and not 'because of' it?
6:12.body: Malbim says בעבור and בגלל differ: בגלל names a cause that comes first, בעבור a purpose that follows. So the blessing came for the ark's benefit, to clear its name as a killer.

sources.quote: כי יש הבדל בין בעבור ובין בגלל, שמלת בגלל מציין הסבה הקודמת ומלת בעבור מציין הסבה המאוחרת
sources.says: Malbim says בגלל marks the earlier cause and בעבור the later one.

sources.quote: להסיר ממנו דבת עם שהוא ממית
sources.says: Malbim says the blessing removed the people's talk that the ark kills.

6:14.headline: Dancing, or praising? Rashi and the Targum differ
6:14.body: Rashi says מכרכר means he danced, and Metzudat Zion calls it a dance of joy. The Targum translates it 'praised', as Radak notes.

sources.quote: מְכַרְכֵּר. מְרַקֵּד
sources.says: Rashi says מכרכר means dancing.

sources.quote: ענין רקידה של שמחה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is a dance of joy.

sources.quote: מרקד בכל כחו וכוונתו
sources.says: Radak says it means dancing with all his strength and purpose, and adds that the Targum has 'praising'.

sources.quote: וְדָוִד מְשַׁבַּח בְּכָל תְּקוֹף
sources.says: The Targum says David was praising with all strength.

6:14.headline: An 'ephod' that Radak says was not the priest's ephod
6:14.body: אפוד is the name of a priest's garment. Radak says this linen ephod was not priestly, so anyone could wear it, while Metzudat David says it was made like the high priest's ephod.

sources.quote: ולא היה מבגדי כהונה לפיכך היה מותר כל אדם ללובשו
sources.says: Radak says it was not a priestly garment, so anyone was allowed to wear it.

sources.quote: אֵפוֹד בָּד. מְעִיל בּוּץ
sources.says: Rashi says אפוד בד is a linen robe.

sources.quote: מלבוש עשוי כדמות האפוד של כהן גדול
sources.says: Metzudat David says it was a garment made like the high priest's ephod.

6:19.headline: אשפר: a sixth of an ox, or just a fine portion?
6:19.body: Rashi, from the Talmud, reads אשפר as 'one of six' parts of an ox. Radak says it packs three words into one, while Metzudat Zion and Ralbag read it as a fine portion, from the root for 'beautiful'.

sources.quote: אֶחָד מִשִּׁשָּׁה בְּפַר
sources.says: Rashi says אשפר means one of six parts of an ox.

sources.quote: אשפר פי' מלה מורכבת משמות ג'
sources.says: Radak says אשפר is a word built from three words.

sources.quote: מנה יפה בשר, והוא מלשון
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is a fine portion of meat, from the language of 'beautiful words' in Genesis.

sources.quote: וענינו מענין שפרה עלי
sources.says: Ralbag says its sense comes from the word for 'beautiful'.

6:23.headline: Until the day she died, or up to and including it?
6:23.body: Rashi and Radak read it as: from that day on, Michal had no child. Radak also gives a midrash that on the day she died she did have one.

sources.quote: לֹא הָיָה לָהּ יָלֶד. מֵאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם וָהָלְאָה
sources.says: Rashi says she had no child from that day on.

sources.quote: מהיום ההוא ואילך לא היה לה
sources.says: Radak says the sages explained that from that day on she had none, as a punishment.

sources.quote: ובדרש אבל ביום המיתה היה לה
sources.says: Radak says a midrash holds that on the day of her death she did have a child.
